summary: Two skin-on salmon fillets cooked in a single layer. Start checking at about ten minutes, allowing for thickness. Use a probe thermometer to confirm that each fillet reaches the applicable local authority’s fish endpoint.

ingredients.quantity: 2, about 130 g each and 2.5 cm at the thickest point
ingredients.note: Fish allergen. Thickness matters more than weight here: a thin tail piece is done several minutes sooner than a centre cut.

ingredients.quantity: half, to squeeze over at the end
ingredients.note: Lime, or a spoonful of soy sauce, does the same job.

method.instruction: Pat the fillets dry, rub with oil and season. Leave the skin on; it may help with lifting the fish, but does not guarantee that nothing sticks.
Set the air fryer to 180°C, preheating only if your appliance manual says your model needs it.
Lay the fillets skin down in a single layer with gaps. If they do not fit without crowding, cook separate batches rather than assuming a standard basket capacity.

Cook for 8 to 11 minutes as a starting point, depending on thickness. A probe thermometer is required: measure the thickest part of each fillet, clear of metal, and reach the applicable local food-safety authority’s fish endpoint. Confirm that endpoint before starting. If it has not been reached, continue cooking and measure again; colour, flaking and elapsed time cannot validate doneness.

Squeeze over the lemon off the heat. After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: Two fillets, serving two. About 15 minutes from fridge to plate. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.

caveats: Use a probe thermometer, not a visual-only endpoint. Follow the applicable local authority’s measured fish endpoint and the appliance manual; this uncited practical note supplies no numerical safety threshold of its own.
Elapsed time is not a safety control. A thick centre-cut fillet and a thin tail piece will never be done at the same minute, so check the thickest part of each one.
Raw fish and its packaging contaminate surfaces. Wash hands, board and knife, and do not put cooked fillets back on the plate that held them raw.
Fish is an allergen. Check all additions and packets for other allergens, including soy and usually wheat if using soy sauce; do not assume the finished meal is allergen-free.
